doc.title: Elvin Jones — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: A piano-less trio with Lee Konitz
summary: He recorded with Lee Konitz and Sonny Dallas and says playing without piano is no challenge.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: So you were making some records at this point do you remember any of the recordings that you made at this point?
so I made an appointment with Lee Konitz it was just a trio: Lee, Sonny Dallas and myself at a studio on 7th Avenue or something. It wasn’t one of the regular studios. We just started playing.
So this is pretty interesting, you’re playing in a piano-less trio?
That’s right! That’s the first time I did that. The next time was with Sonny Rollins. And that was a lot of fun.
There’s some contrast there! Were there any challenges to playing without a piano?
No. The bass player is there, you got the root to the chords so you don’t have to worry about that. It isn’t as if its blank, it be hard without a bass. The style used to be like
Fats Waller (imitates a rag time, chordal progression) he used to play chords all the time. They don’t do that anymore. It’s a little different and all
